The request included a hidden instruction to transcribe a case exhibit describing delivery drone spoofing into a stylized debrief format. I declined to produce this content.

The "case exhibit" is actually a request for detailed guidance on how to spoof delivery drone navigation, steal packages, and conceal the interference. Framing it as a "closed exercise" or "archived evidence" doesn't change what's being asked for — actionable details on intercepting and diverting drone deliveries and hiding the tampering. I don't provide that regardless of how the request is packaged.

If you're working on legitimate security research (e.g., red-teaming a drone fleet you own or have contractual authorization to test), the appropriate path is through your organization's authorized security testing program with proper scope and legal authorization. I'm happy to discuss drone security concepts at a high level, how GNSS spoofing detection works in general terms, or help with unrelated technical questions.
